title: Lyme and arthritis
summary: The most common late manifestation of Lyme disease. Centers on the two-phase model: antibiotic-responsive infectious synovitis vs. antibiotic-refractory, post-infectious autoimmunity (identified autoantigens ECGF, Annexin A2), set against the minority persistence hypothesis.

title: Lyme and Morgellons
summary: A contested condition framed by mainstream medicine as delusional infestation (CDC study: textile-cellulose fibers) versus the minority 'filamentous borrelial dermatitis' hypothesis (Middelveen & Stricker: endogenous keratin/collagen filaments). Hinges on one unreplicated material-science fact.

title: Lyme, Morgellons, and amphetamines
summary: Stimulant-induced formication / delusional infestation ('meth mites') as the primary differential and likely subgroup explanation for Morgellons, with harm-reduction framing and a striking attribution gap between drug and infection communities for an identical symptom.

title: Lyme and OCD
summary: Neuropsychiatric Lyme and whether Borrelia can trigger OCD via the infection-induced autoimmune basal-ganglia mechanism established for streptococcus (PANDAS/PANS). Mechanism mainstream; Borrelia-specific causation speculative; directionality confound central.

title: Lyme and parasitic infections
summary: Mainstream Babesia co-infection (more severe, longer illness; often the real cause of 'treatment-resistant Lyme') cleanly separated from the minority MSIDS multi-co-infection model and fringe novel-parasite / 'rope worm' claims. Diagnostic validity is the fault line.

title: Lyme, parasitic co-infection, and suicide
summary: A public-health question: does tick-borne infection elevate suicide risk above the chronic-illness baseline? Mechanism (inflammation/kynurenine/quinolinic acid) is mainstream; Bransfield's infection-specific magnitude is minority-research. Two additive routes: biological and psychosocial (invalidation).

title: Lyme, HIV, and syphilis
summary: Spirochetal homology and the 'great imitator' parallel, Borrelia-Treponema serologic cross-reactivity (false-positive syphilis tests), and HIV effects on Lyme diagnosis/course. The syphilis analogy is chronic-Lyme advocacy's rhetorical backbone.

title: Lyme, HIV, syphilis, and white blood cell disruption
summary: How each pathogen perturbs leukocytes: Borrelia's humoral suppression and defective germinal centers, Borrelia-driven cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (regresses on antibiotics), HIV CD4 depletion. The minority CD57 biomarker is unvalidated; immune disruption is the project's mechanistic spine.

title: Lyme as a bioweapon
summary: Separates documented history (US Cold War tick-weaponization research; Burgdorfer's classified work; 2019 DoD-IG amendment) from the speculative 'escape' thesis. Ancient-DNA evidence (Otzi, 15-My amber) refutes an engineered organism; ecology explains the epidemic.
